name: compact-tablet-navbar
goal: Keep branch, commit and search controls compact and usable across tablet widths.

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: Tablet revision and search controls use at most 120 pixels; Branch and Commit share a row with accessible 44-pixel controls.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: Existing shell search-fit coverage checks overlap and preserved widths, not toolbar height. Extend its width matrix to 685, 834 and 1024 and add compactness assertions.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: Red 7bef4f65 at 1952fe51 fails the 120-pixel tablet toolbar bound and narrow-tablet row alignment. Frozen tests and environment are preserved.

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
steps.evidence: Codex fallback updated only two existing stylesheets after Opus returned no edits in seven minutes. Three focused tablet browser cases pass with unchanged tests.

steps.title: Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
steps.evidence: Red 7bef4f65 at 1952fe51 and green 8c31aed0 at 2c42b873 share 1,257 frozen inputs and environment. All three tablet cases pass unchanged.

steps.title: Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
